items.context: A theatre review published on a website

items.prompt: The play, set in 1930s Vienna, ___ the audience from the very first scene.

explanation.en: Grip means to hold someone's attention completely. Holds up means to delay, and catches does not fit with an audience.

items.prompt: The lead actor, ___ performance has already won several awards, is superb as the old king.

explanation.en: Whose shows possession: the actor's performance. Which is for things, and of whom cannot stand before a noun in this way.

items.prompt: By the time the curtain came down, most of the audience ___ to their feet.

explanation.en: By the time + past simple needs the past perfect for the action completed before it: had leapt. Has leapt is present perfect, which cannot follow a past time clause, and leap is present simple.

items.prompt: It is a production that is well ___ seeing, whatever your usual taste in theatre.

explanation.en: Worth is followed directly by an -ing form: worth seeing. Worthwhile and worthy cannot be used this way.
explanation.es: «Vale la pena verla» es «worth seeing», sin «of» ni «to».

items.prompt: I would strongly advise anyone with an interest in modern drama ___ a seat early.

explanation.en: Advise + person + to + infinitive is the correct pattern. Advise booking would need no person before it.
